mission_phase: Generation 11 - High Country Owner Outreach Product Discovery Report
focus: Reframe the High Country Outfitters deliverable from a scorecard-style assessment into an owner-facing customer-experience opportunity report that answers how to make it easier for customers to find and buy products, with a full experiment reference dataset, expanded IR concept coverage, Spanish/bilingual discovery, same-query competitor evidence, and organic/paid-placement caveats in references.
reason_generation_started: User clarified that the report needed stronger executive presentation, 25 examples per discovery concept, no article references, no scorecard framing, Spanish/bilingual discovery, at least two competitor evaluations, and a careful organic versus paid-placement opportunity story.
reason_generation_ended: The owner-outreach JSON, Markdown, LaTeX, PDF, expanded evidence artifact with same-query competitor benchmark, customer-experience-first executive narrative, final page 3 customer-effort visual, validators, handoffs, and MDE records were created and validated with two clean local Validation Gate passes. The final design refinement reviewed pages 1-3 as executive slides, addressed page 3 whitespace with visual communication from saved GEN-011 evidence only, and did not run a new ecommerce evaluation.

validators.execution_note: Compiled the Northvalley owner-outreach PDF to 30 pages after the same-query competitor refinement.

validators.tool: pdfinfo / pdftotext / pdftoppm / rendered page spot check
validators.category: Usability / UI Standards / Content Integrity Validation
validators.execution_note: PDF text includes customer-experience framing, 175 target experiments, same-query competitor references, High Country-first executive pages, Spanish/bilingual discovery, paid-placement caveats, the page 3 customer-effort visual labels, and no visible article-reference, scorecard framing, old executive ranking language, or technical-first executive narrative. Rendered cover and first two numbered pages were spot-checked after the customer-experience rewrite, then pages 1-3 were reviewed again after the final slide-design pass.

Validator now requires the executive competitor context JSON/text, customer-experience language, High Country-first consulting language, qualitative peer-reference framing, and exclusion of old trails/leads/top-performer and technical-first executive language.

evidence_quality_notes: GEN-011 uses saved public evidence and a fresh expanded IR/competitor evidence artifact; no sibling repository files were changed.
175 search/autocomplete examples were evaluated: 25 each for Normalization, Tokenization, Synonyms, Ranking And Field Weighting, Query Expansion, Document Enrichment, and Spanish/Bilingual Discovery.
Search averaged 94/100, autocomplete averaged 45/100, and uniform search/autocomplete assistance appeared in 43% of examples.
Spanish/bilingual discovery is framed as market access, not demographic labeling. It averaged 86/100 in rendered search and 0/100 in autocomplete.

Half-Moon Outfitters and Mast General Store each produced 175/175 usable rendered search rows and 175/175 public suggest rows using the same protected query set as High Country. Competitor checks are opportunity framing and framework benchmarks, not market-share proof.

No visible paid-placement labels were found in the sampled competitor rendered text, but this is not proof paid placement or retail media does not exist. Organic/paid discussion now lives in reference, not the executive readout.

The executive summary now presents High Country as the hero: it emphasizes a strong online shopping foundation and customer product-finding experience, treats comparable regional retailers as reference examples, avoids saying a competitor is better in the executive pages, and keeps exact peer scores in references.

The customer-experience executive narrative follow-up was rebuilt from saved GEN-011 evidence only; no new live evaluation, unsupported competitor claim, market-share claim, or confidential revenue claim was added.

The final executive page design follow-up reviewed pages 1-3 as slides and addressed page 3 whitespace with a before/after Customer Effort Reduction Model, Business Value Lens, 90-Day Opportunity Roadmap, and Executive Decision Focus strip rather than additional paragraphs.
The 1-4% conservative and 3-7% stretch sales upside ranges are directional models only because High Country analytics and revenue data were not available.
The report intentionally removes visible article references and scorecard framing; detailed experiments remain in the reference appendix.

top_findings.summary: Search is strong after submit, but autocomplete does not uniformly support the same shopper language.
Spanish and mixed Spanish-English terms often recover products in search but had no autocomplete assistance in the 25-example set.

Two relevant outdoor retail benchmarks produced same-query rendered search and public suggest evidence across all 175 protected examples; the executive pages now use those competitors only as reference examples while keeping exact measurements in references.
The requested competitor comparison belonged in a visible first-page executive section, not only as an inline paragraph and reference appendix.

The opening pages needed to sound like an experienced advisory conversation starter about making it easier for customers to find and buy products, not a competitor ranking, search-technology audit, or framework proof.
The Recommended Growth Path page needed a decision-supporting visual to address whitespace and read more like a consulting slide.

next_recommended_action: Review the 30-page owner-outreach PDF as a President/GM conversation starter. The first three pages now read as presentation-style executive pages; page 3 uses a customer-effort visual and 90-Day Opportunity Roadmap to support a 30-minute conversation.
